name: Workspace369
tagline: A bundled online workspace that puts docs, tasks, and shared files behind one login.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Bundled workspace products are wide rather than deep, and width is exactly what an agent handles well: docs, a task board, file uploads, and search are all boring, well trodden CRUD. A single session gets you a local app that covers your own notes and tasks convincingly. What it does not get you is the part that makes a workspace a workspace: other people in it, permissions that you trust, real time editing, and a mobile client you do not hate. If you are the only user, the SaaS is mostly paying for hosting and a login screen. If you have a team, the bundle stops being a feature list and starts being shared habit, which is not something you build on a Saturday.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with markdown docs, a drag and drop task board, file attachments, and full text search across all of it, stored in one SQLite file.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine that stays on, or a cheap VPS
A backup habit for the SQLite file and uploads directory
Tailscale or similar if you want phone access without exposing a port
whatYouLose: Multiplayer: real time co-editing, comments, presence, and any notion of who changed what
Permissions and sharing that you would be comfortable giving a client or contractor
Polished mobile and offline access instead of a browser tab pointed at your LAN
Integrations: calendar sync, email, storage providers, single sign on
Someone else owning uptime, backups, and the migration when your schema was wrong
moatNotes: The lock in is not the feature list, it is that six months of your team's documents and task history live inside it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody buys an all-in-one workspace because any single module is hard. They buy it because one bill, one login, and one place to look beats stitching four tools together, and because the moment a second person needs access, self hosting turns into an admin job with permissions, invites, and a support queue of one. For a solo user the paid version is largely convenience. For anything with coworkers or clients, paying is cheaper than becoming the IT department.
notes: Solo, the DIY version is genuinely fine; add one coworker and the maths flips fast.
prompt:
Build a single user, self hosted personal workspace app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/workspace.db
- Local filesystem uploads in ./data/uploads
- No external APIs, no auth provider, no analytics

Features in scope:
1. Docs: create, rename, delete markdown documents. Editor is a plain textarea with a live preview toggle. Autosave on a 600ms debounce. Docs can be nested one level under a folder name.
2. Tasks: a board with columns Todo, Doing, Done. Drag and drop between columns, inline title edit, due date, optional link to a doc. Persist column order.
3. Files: drag and drop upload, stored on disk, row in SQLite with original filename, size, mime type, created date. Download and delete.
4. Search: one search box in the header that does full text search across doc titles, doc bodies, task titles, and filenames using SQLite FTS5. Results grouped by type, keyboard navigable.
5. Home: a dashboard listing tasks due in the next 7 days and the 5 most recently edited docs.

Out of scope, do not build: multi user, sharing links, permissions, real time collaboration, comments, mobile app, rich text WYSIWYG, calendar sync, email.

Requirements:
- Everything must work offline on localhost with `npm run dev`
- Include `npm run backup` that zips ./data with a timestamped filename
- Migrations run automatically on boot, idempotent
- Seed script with 3 sample docs, 6 tasks, and 1 uploaded text file
- Any config goes in .env with a checked in .env.example, and .env stays gitignored
- README: how to run it, where the data lives, how to back it up, and a blunt note that this app has no auth so do not expose it to the internet without a VPN or reverse proxy
